edges.note: Romanticism defines itself against neoclassical reason, order, and restraint
Gothic revives the irrational and medieval against Enlightenment rationalism
Gothic terror and the sublime feed the "dark Romantic" imagination
Transmitted largely via Poe; morbidity and beauty-in-decay
Poe, in Baudelaire's translations, shapes the Symbolist imagination
Realism rejects Romantic idealization for ordinary social life
The American branch of Romanticism (Emerson via German and English Romantics)
Romantic subjectivity carried forward through Baudelaire
Keatsian autonomy of beauty seeds "art for art's sake"
Zola radicalizes Realism with determinism and heredity
Modernism breaks with realist convention while inheriting its craft
Determinism and documentary detail feed early Modernist fiction
Closely allied; shared figures (Baudelaire, Huysmans, Mallarmé)
Autonomy of art (Wilde, Pater) feeds Modernist aesthetics
The crucial bridge to Modernist poetry (Yeats, Eliot, Pound)
Imagism rejects Symbolist vagueness while descending from it
Rimbaud and Lautreamont revered as Surrealist ancestors
The first phase of Anglo-American poetic Modernism
Postmodernism continues and reacts against Modernist form
Modernist alienation (Kafka, Dostoevsky) shapes Existentialist fiction
Shared moment; Modernist form in Toomer's Cane
Beckett is the hinge between Modernism and the Absurd
Kafka and Borges supply much of the technique
Modernist technique adapted by postcolonial writers
Carpentier among the Paris Surrealists; "lo real maravilloso"
Irrationality and play feed postmodern experiment
Automatism and spontaneity influence Beat method
Dream logic and absurdity feed Absurdist theatre
Whitman and self-reliance channelled by Ginsberg and the Beats
Absurdist drama stages the existential and absurd condition (Camus)
Postwar alienation and radical freedom
Directly inspires Negritude (Cesaire, Senghor), a root of Postcolonial literature
Metatheatre and meaninglessness feed postmodern drama (Stoppard)
Burroughs's cut-up method claimed by both
Garcia Marquez and Rushdie shared by both
Rushdie, Okri, and Morrison work across both
Much postcolonial fiction adopts postmodern strategies
